items.title: read_csv treats leading zeros as VARCHAR during type auto-detection
items.body:
### What happens?

When reading a CSV file that has values like `01` and `12`, the auto-detected type for the column ends up being `VARCHAR`, when I expected it to ignore leading zeros and detect `Integer` instead.

Example:
The `fips` column in the NYTimes US COVID data repository contains these identifiers with leading zeros.
- https://github.com/nytimes/covid-19-data/blob/master/us-states.csv

Do you think it's reasonable to detect an `Integer` type in cases like this?

### To Reproduce

_Using a downloaded copy of this file:_
<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nytimes/covid-19-data/master/us-states.csv>

```python
import duckdb
conn = duckdb.connect()
rel = conn.read_csv("us-states.csv")
rel.show()
```

### OS:

Darwin, macOS 14.4, aarch64 (arm64)

### DuckDB Version:

v0.9.2

Python
